title: Chapter 177: He's Inside the Door
html:
“The door?” Men Nan’s voice changed audibly. The word had stirred something in him. He owned a copy of the photograph Chen Ge had sent, but kept it buried beneath several books at the bottom of a drawer.

That had puzzled Chen Ge when he saw the picture at Hai Ming Apartments. It was Men Nan’s only photograph of his mother, yet instead of displaying it in a frame, he had hidden it in a remote corner like a memory he refused to confront.

He could neither throw it away nor bear to face it. The photograph embodied the conflict within him.

“Where did you get this picture?” Men Nan’s voice grew hoarse, his words slowing. Chen Ge had dragged what he wanted to bury back into the light, leaving him nowhere to hide.

“I found the picture at the mental hospital. I’ve gone inside the room your mother stayed in…”

“Leave that place immediately!” Men Nan screamed before Chen Ge finished.

“Leave? It sounds as though you remember something.”

Silence settled over the line again. Several seconds later, Men Nan said, “I don’t know why I said that. My instincts just tell me that place is extremely dangerous.”

“The hospital is locked, and I can’t get out. If this weren’t urgent, I wouldn’t have disturbed you.” Cleaver in hand, Chen Ge watched the blood vessels continue creeping toward Zhang Ya. “This is bigger than either of us. The madmen who refused treatment have returned with all their twisted beliefs. They’ve imprisoned living people and experimented on them with axes and saws. Can you imagine what else they might have done?”

“There are victims inside the hospital?” Uncertainty filled Men Nan’s voice. He seemed to doubt himself, as though he had something to say but could not muster the courage.

“I can confirm there’s more than one. I’ve found ample evidence of multiple victims.” Chen Ge could not understand Men Nan’s hesitation. “And I’m in danger myself. Monsters and axe-wielding patients are hunting me. There’s no reasoning with them.”

After a long silence, Men Nan asked, “How do you expect me to help?”

“Awaken the other persona inside you. He’s the one I need!” The stench in the corridor thickened, as though some enormous monster had opened its jaws.

“Can you tell me why?” Men Nan asked softly, his voice heavy with conflicting emotions.

Chen Ge had no time for evasions, so he told him the truth. “I need to close the door in Room 3 of the Third Sick Hall. Your childhood persona knows how. Wake him up! I know what happened when you were young. I understand your pain, but you can’t run from it forever!”

“Close the door…” Men Nan sounded as though he were speaking to himself. “I’m sorry, but I’m afraid I can’t help you.”

The blunt refusal caught Chen Ge off guard. “Why not?”

“Because he is not with me.” Men Nan took a deep breath. “He locked himself up behind the door.”

“Your childhood persona is on the other side of the door?” Chen Ge’s brow knotted.

“Yes. In truth, he is the original personality. My own memories begin after the age of four.” Men Nan continued with a shocking revelation. “The original personality was born in that mental hospital and grew up believing its distortions were normal. His world was nothing like everyone else’s. During those first four years, he struggled to correct his perspective, and his mother was his only source of support. But when he was four, she was murdered. He witnessed everything and abandoned the normal world.

“Perhaps the normal world had never shown him any kindness. He came to believe that our world was the truly distorted one. He withdrew into the deepest part of our mind, and then I appeared. He never communicated with me until the hospital director and a Doctor Chen came looking for me. They begged me to help close this ‘door.’

“I was so young then. Without explaining anything, they took me back to the mental hospital where the original personality had spent his childhood. They asked me question after question, none of which I could answer now.

“That night, they put me to bed in Room 3. I don’t know what happened next. There were probably sleeping pills in the water because I slept unnaturally deeply. That must have been when they summoned the original personality.

“By the time I woke, it was already midnight. I opened my eyes groggily and found myself lying on the bed, but everything around me was blood red. Stranger still, the original personality was standing at my bedside.

“He told me to keep what happened secret from everyone and pointed to the clock in the corridor. He said I had to remain awake no matter how tired I became. Then he sent me out of the room. He stayed behind the door and closed it.

“He hasn’t appeared since. Sometimes, though, memories that aren’t mine surface in my consciousness. I intended to take these secrets to my grave because even now, I can’t be certain they aren’t hallucinations.

“My condition resembles schizophrenia, yet everything feels so real. I grew up doubting myself constantly. That’s the main reason I chose to study psychology.”

Pain saturated Men Nan’s voice, and even as an outsider, Chen Ge could understand it. For this young man, pretending to be ordinary and living an ordinary life was a constant struggle.

“That explains why he couldn’t resist the mirror ghost.” Chen Ge clutched the phone, anxiety making his heart tremble.

“Men Nan is likely telling the truth. When I detected the third persona in his psyche, it did resemble a collection of shattered memories. The episodes were fragmented and appeared at random.” Doctor Gao had taken the phone from Men Nan. He did not understand much of their conversation and could offer little help.

“Yes, he should be telling the truth.”

The only person capable of closing the door had spent more than a decade behind it—the same length of time it had remained shut. Only when the hospital closed five years ago had the door opened again. Had something happened to the original Men Nan inside?

Chen Ge wanted to retreat. The building was too sinister; even with Zhang Ya beside him, he felt far from safe. “Retreating is the safest choice.”

He turned toward the corridor. A draft stirred Zhang Ya’s red dress. Her black hair merged with the darkness and repeatedly pierced the monsters’ bodies. Two of the three creatures had already been torn apart.
